idiom_name: caller-owned error list (struct notification) + checks that append
implementation_notes: C has no exceptions, so the pattern's structure is the only option but must be built by hand: declare a struct that owns a bounded array of entries plus a count, pass a pointer to it into every check, and let each check append instead of returning early; the checks return void (or a status for fatal faults that must still abort the pass) and the caller inspects count/entries. Store an error code plus the field name rather than a message, or format into a caller-provided buffer with snprintf; errno is a single-value convention and cannot carry several failures.
pitfalls: A fixed-capacity array must refuse or drop overflow deterministically; silently truncating diagnostics hides failures.
The notification must be owned by the caller and passed explicitly to every helper - a global or static accumulator is not thread-safe and leaks errors across requests.
A helper that returns early while holding a lock or an open resource (or longjmps out of it) reintroduces the fail-fast path the struct exists to replace.
